# Transformer results (DistilBERT + LoRA, 6-month data)

*Numbers auto-generated by notebook 04b on Colab (device: cuda, max_length = 256,
batch = 32, early stopping, max 6 epochs / patience 2). Comparison section added
by hand so the report is fair and self-contained. Full narrative and the ship
decision are in `reports/transformer_vs_baseline.md` and `reports/model_card.md`.*

## Fair comparison — vs the 6-month baseline (same natural test set)

This is the comparison that matters: both models scored on the same natural
34,694-row test set.

**Task A — product classification (9 classes, macro-F1)**

| model | macro-F1 | accuracy |
|---|---|---|
| 6-month baseline (LogReg word+char) | 0.7065 | 0.8337 |
| DistilBERT + LoRA, Tier 1 (plain_ce, r=16) | **0.7386** | 0.8537 |

Tier 1 transformer wins product by ~3 points. (The earlier naive run scored
0.6832 and lost; see `transformer_vs_baseline.md`.)

**Task B — monetary relief (binary, ~3% positive)**

| model | PR-AUC | ROC-AUC |
|---|---|---|
| 6-month baseline (LogReg word+char) | **0.3337** | 0.9396 |
| DistilBERT + LoRA, Tier 1 (focal) | 0.3308 | 0.9401 |

Tied, baseline a nose ahead.

**Validation (Tier 1, for model selection):** product plain_ce val macro-F1 0.7473
(vs focal 0.7302); monetary focal val PR-AUC 0.3548 (vs weighted_ce 0.3519).

## Serving cost

On the T4 the transformer runs at ~0.2 ms/complaint, but that requires a GPU and
the full PyTorch + Transformers + PEFT stack. The baseline scores a median-length
complaint in about 2.8 ms on a 2-thread **CPU** (under 1 ms per complaint in
batches; `reports/latency_report.md`) as a single scikit-learn pickle. The real cost difference
is operational — GPU + heavy runtime vs a tiny CPU model — not raw per-item
latency on a GPU. That cost is why the baseline still ships despite losing on
product.
